references.text: Saul swears that not a hair of Jonathan's head shall fall to the ground – an expression of God's complete protection. The same imagery Jesus uses in [ref:Luk 21:18|Luke 21:18] to assure his disciples of God's care.
The woman from Tekoa uses the expression that not a hair shall fall to the ground ([ref:2 Sam 14:11|2 Samuel 14:11]), emphasizing God's total protection – the same image Jesus uses.
Solomon promises that not a hair of Adonijah's head shall fall if he proves worthy ([ref:1 Kong 1:52|1 Kings 1:52]). The same idiom regarding God's preserving care.

Jesus says that all the hairs on his disciples' heads are numbered ([ref:Matt 10:30|Matthew 10:30]), expressing God's detailed care and knowledge of his children – a direct parallel to the promise in [ref:Luk 21:18|Luke 21:18].

Jesus says that even the hairs on his disciples' heads are numbered ([ref:Luk 12:7|Luke 12:7]). Luke uses this motif twice – here in connection with not fearing people, and in [ref:Luk 21:18|Luke 21:18] in connection with end-time persecution.

Paul uses exactly the same expression that not a hair shall be lost from anyone's head ([ref:Apg 27:34|Acts 27:34]), during the storm at sea. This shows that the promise of God's protection was carried forward in apostolic preaching.
